# Rovara

> Rovara is an open-source coding agent you install in your own AWS account. People ask it for work in Slack, or from Claude Code, Codex or Cursor; it works on the project's repositories in an isolated EC2 workspace, checks the result and opens pull requests. The npm package `@preplabsai/rovara-code` installs the `rovara` command and its alias `agentx` (the same program; the docs write `agentx`), which installs and runs an environment: projects, Slack channels, connectors, settings, upgrades.

Notes for agents driving the CLI:

- Always pass `--env <name>`. Without it, `agentx` uses the environment named `production`.
- Pass `--json` to get `{"ok":true,"data":...}` or `{"ok":false,"error":{"code","message"}}` on stdout. Progress goes to stderr. Exit codes are listed in the CLI reference.
- Commands that change projects, channels and connectors need an admin sign-in, which a person completes once in a browser: `agentx --env <name> login --admin`.
- With no terminal, some yes/no questions are currently answered yes on their own (issue #1595). Answer them with flags; the CLI reference lists which.
- Pass secrets as `--<name>-file <path>` or `--<name>-env <NAME>`, never as values on the command line.
- Pages marked "maintainers" describe the Rovara maintainers' own deployment. Skip them when working on an environment installed with `agentx init`.

## Start here

- [CLI reference](docs/cli-reference.md): `--env`, credentials, JSON output, exit codes, behaviour without a terminal, recipes, and the commands with their flags
- [Install overview](docs/getting-started.md): `agentx init`, the commands after the install, and developer sign-in on one page
- [How Rovara works](docs/how-it-works.md): the request path, the check report, context files and stack names

## Install and run an environment

- [Installing Rovara](docs/install.md): the Launch in AWS button, installing from a terminal, the install page, unattended `--yes` installs
- [Other ways to install](docs/install-advanced.md): CDK, a platform team's export, a source checkout
- [Running Rovara](docs/day-two.md): the operator role, `doctor`, `upgrade`, `config`, projects, channels and connectors
- [Removing an environment](docs/teardown.md): `agentx destroy`
- [Moving accounts](docs/move-account.md): moving an environment to another AWS account

## Projects, Slack channels and connectors

- [Project configuration](docs/project-configuration.md): every field of a project file, setup and readiness commands, and how checks work
- [Working in Slack](docs/slack.md): threads, confirmations, connector credentials, shared tasks, diagnostics
- [Companies and projects](docs/company-and-projects.md): creating projects and linking channels through company sign-in instead of the CLI
- [Linear](docs/connectors/linear.md), [Jira](docs/connectors/jira.md), [Asana](docs/connectors/asana.md), [any MCP server](docs/connectors/custom-mcp.md): credentials and setup per connector
- [Channel adapters](docs/channel-adapters.md): WhatsApp and other channels through the channel API
- [Pull requests](docs/pull-requests.md): publishing, GitHub App permissions, CodeBuild gates

## Developers

- [Use Rovara from your AI tool](docs/mcp-install.md): `agentx mcp install` for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor
- [Sign-in clients](docs/sign-in-clients.md): letting another service, such as a dashboard or a channel adapter, sign people in with Rovara
- [Sign in with ChatGPT](docs/chatgpt.md): running your tasks on your own ChatGPT plan
- [Rovara loop](docs/loop.md): Rovara's workflow on your GitHub issues, run locally
